chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Ibrahim al-Sindi, from Yahya al-Azraq, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) dug a well, so they threw (things) into it. He was informed of that, so he came until he stood over it and said: 'You should refrain, or I will dwell the pigeons in it.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The swishing of their wings repels the devils.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali put pigeons in the well and what is the spiritual significance of their wings?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical wisdom of Imam Ali (AS) in utilizing pigeons not merely for sustenance but for their spiritual utility, specifically their ability to repel *Shayatin* (devils) through the sound of their wings. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elaborates on this metaphysical benefit, illustrating the Shia tradition's view of the natural world as a means of spiritual protection and purification. The narration underscores the interconnectedness of physical actions and spiritual states in the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt.
